# tmux-skills

> Codex skill for controlled tmux usage, managed watch/queue workers, visible status records, and real-use tmux E2E validation.

Bridge wakeup adds a path-only app-server notification flow for dormant main Codex threads. Treat the PoC same-thread wake fixture as the hard gate before relying on daemon lifecycle commands.

Use this file as the LLM entry point. Start with the core files for orientation, then read the detailed docs only for the behavior you need to modify or verify.

## Core

- [README](README.md): Project overview, requirements, file map, and verification entry points.
- [Skill instructions](SKILL.md): Agent operating guide for choosing panes, sending commands, capturing output, and using tmux safely.

## Detailed docs

- [Docs index](docs/README.md): LLM wiki map and maintenance rules for README, SKILL, docs, and references.
- [LLM wiki style guide](docs/llm-wiki-style-guide.md): Rules for writing canonical, low-duplication, code-fact-checked wiki pages.
- [Workflows and features](docs/workflows-and-features.md): Desired operating flow, feature map, and workflow-to-test mapping.
- [Managed workers](docs/managed-workers.md): Canonical contract for `watch`, `queue-after-idle`, `queue-after-status`, dedupe, stale GC, send preflight behavior, and the bridge boundary.
- [Real-use E2E](docs/real-use-e2e.md): Canonical guide for `scripts/e2e_real_use.py`, smoke/all scenario groups, exit codes, diagnostics, and cleanup checks.

## References

- [Workflows](references/WORKFLOWS.md): Copyable tmux-skills workflow examples for long-running jobs, resume, monitors, and output review.

## Optional

No optional docs are required for normal agent execution yet.
